welcome: Welcome to D.O.lfine, a quiet place to practise reading, rhythm and harmony. Choose a module below, set it as you like, and start. In music theory and ear training, levels open one by one as your answers improve.
settings_lede: Shared by every module. Saved in this browser only.
sight_reading_lede: Fresh, graded exercises, read at tempo. Dandelot-style at the easier levels.
results_heard_hint: Under a wrong note, in red: what was heard or played instead.
results_unscored: Done. Without a MIDI keyboard this run was not scored; take the next one while you’re warm.
commentary_clean: Clean and steady. Try the next level, or raise the tempo here.
commentary_pitches: Most slips were wrong notes. Use the preview to find the tricky bars, and read one beat ahead.
commentary_late: Notes tended to land late. Keep going after a mistake rather than correcting it.
commentary_rush: Notes tended to rush. Let the metronome lead, and breathe on long notes.
rhythm_lede: Jazz rhythm reading after Freddy Roux’s Rhythm’n Jazz, and polyrhythm. Practice mode: the app keeps time, you perform.
modulation_lede: Two bars at the old tempo, then two at the new one. Hold the new pulse yourself if the metronome drops out.
theory_lede: Jazz harmony at the keyboard: the major, melodic minor and harmonic minor scales, their modes, voicings and voice leading.

guide_sight_reading_intro_p1: Every exercise here is new: generated from the level you choose, so it can never be learnt by heart. Read it as you would at an exam or a first rehearsal: look it over, then play it through without stopping.
guide_sight_reading_intro_p2: Levels run from 1 to 10 and are roughly mapped to ABRSM grades and French conservatoire cycles. The mapping is a guide to place yourself, not a certification.
guide_sight_reading_dandelot_p1: In the spirit of Dandelot, reading starts from a few landmarks: the clef’s own note (G on the treble clef, F on the bass clef) and middle C. Every other note is read by its distance from the nearest landmark, not decoded line by line.
guide_sight_reading_dandelot_p2: At the easier levels these reference notes are highlighted in the score. Find them first during the preview; the rest of the line hangs from them.
guide_sight_reading_technique_p1: Scan the key and time signature first, then the shape of the line: where it climbs, where it leaps, where the rhythm gets busy. Mark the tricky bars in your head.
guide_sight_reading_technique_p2: When you play, keep going. A wrong note is one note; stopping costs the bar. Let your eyes stay a beat ahead of your hands.
guide_sight_reading_modes_p1: Performance mode is the real thing: a preview, a count-in, then the music runs at tempo and nothing waits for you. With a MIDI keyboard every note is scored.
guide_sight_reading_modes_p2: Practice mode takes the clock away. The score stays put, the metronome is optional, and nothing is assessed: use it to work through a key or a rhythm until it feels easy.
guide_rhythm_swing_p1: Written eighths change meaning with the feel. Straight, they split the beat evenly; swung, the first is longer and the second leans into the next beat. The swing ratio says how far: 2:1 is the classic triplet swing.
guide_rhythm_swing_p2: Let the metronome click on 2 and 4, like a drummer’s hi-hat, and feel the long-short pairs settle between the clicks.
guide_rhythm_syllables_p1: Say or sing the syllables under the notes before you clap. Long notes open, short notes stay light, off-beats push forward. When the line sounds right in your voice, it will sound right on your instrument.
guide_rhythm_polyrhythm_p1: Start slowly with one hand at a time against the shared downbeat. Then learn the composite rhythm, the single pattern both hands make together, and only then split it back into two parts.
guide_rhythm_polyrhythm_p2: The circle shows the cycle: both parts start together at the top and meet again there every cycle.
guide_rhythm_modulation_p1: A metric modulation keeps one note value constant while the pulse changes around it. Before the switch, feel the new pulse inside the old one; after it, let the old one go.
guide_theory_intro_p1: Stack thirds on every degree of a parent scale and you get seven modes and seven seventh chords. The major, melodic minor and harmonic minor scales together give the 21 modes most jazz harmony is built from.
guide_theory_intro_p2: Name a mode by its degree and its parent: the Altered scale is the seventh mode of melodic minor, so B Altered lives in C melodic minor.
guide_theory_voicings_p1: Type A puts root and seventh in the left hand, third, fifth and ninth in the right (1 7 / 3 5 9). Type B puts root, third and seventh in the left, ninth and fifth in the right (1 3 7 / 9 5). Alternated from chord to chord they keep the guide tones moving smoothly.
guide_theory_voicings_p2: Six modes need an alternative: Phrygian and Dorian ♭2 become 7sus4(♭9), Locrian takes the 11th instead of the ♭9, Altered uses ♭13 and ♯9, and Ultralocrian takes no tension at all.
guide_theory_voice_leading_p1: Only the bass follows the roots. Every other voice holds its note when the next chord shares it, and otherwise moves by a second at most. Keep the right hand at or below A5 and respect the low interval limits so nothing turns to mud.
guide_ear_intro_p1: Every question starts with a reference: the root for chords and voicings, a drone for modes, the tonic chord for progressions. Name what you hear relative to it.
guide_ear_intro_p2: Replay as often as you need, arpeggiate when a chord is dense, and after each answer listen to your guess and the real thing back to back.
results_stopped: Stopped. Restart from the beginning, or practise it at your own pace.
lessons_lede: How the three parent scales build the chords of jazz harmony, and how a pianist voices them. Read, look at the staff, and listen.
lesson_major_summary: Seven modes, seven chords: Ionian to Locrian.
lesson_melodic_minor_summary: Minor-major, Lydian dominant, Altered and more.
lesson_harmonic_minor_summary: The dominant and the diminished chord of minor keys.
lesson_voicings_summary: Every chord so far, in eight piano voicings you can hear.
lesson_major_p1: Build a seventh chord on every degree of the major scale, using only its notes, and you get the seven chords of the key: Δ7 on I and IV, -7 on II, III and VI, 7 on V, ø7 on VII. Each degree is also a mode: the same seven notes heard from a different root.
lesson_major_p2: Learn each mode with its chord. The characteristic notes are what make a mode sound like itself: the major sixth of Dorian, the sharp fourth of Lydian, the flat seventh of Mixolydian. Play the scale, then the chord, and listen for them.
lesson_melodic_minor_p1: The melodic minor scale, in its jazz form, is the same going up and down: a major scale with a flat third. Its modes give some of the most-used sounds in modern jazz: the minor-major chord, Lydian dominant, and the Altered scale on the seventh degree.
lesson_melodic_minor_p2: Its chords have no avoid notes, so every tension sounds. Many of them are dominant colours: Lydian dominant for 7(♯11), Mixolydian ♭6 for 7(♭13), Altered for 7alt.
lesson_harmonic_minor_p1: The harmonic minor scale raises the seventh of natural minor so that V becomes a dominant chord. The augmented second between the sixth and the seventh gives it its colour.
lesson_harmonic_minor_p2: Its fifth mode, Phrygian dominant, is the V7(♭9 ♭13) of minor keys; its second degree is the half-diminished chord of a minor II–V, and its seventh carries the diminished seventh chord.
lesson_voicings_p1: A chord symbol says which notes to play, not where to put them. These are the classic ways a pianist lays out the same chord, from plain close position to the two-hand voicings used in the exercises.
lesson_voicings_p2: Play each one, then hear them back to back. Listening for the difference trains the ear: the top note and the spacing change the colour as much as the chord itself.
voicing_close_about: The four chord tones stacked in thirds above the root.
voicing_drop2_about: Close position with the second voice from the top dropped an octave: wider, and easy to spread over two hands.
voicing_shell_37_about: Root, third and seventh: the bare frame of the chord, a typical left hand for comping.
voicing_shell_73_about: The same three notes with the seventh below the third. Alternating the two shells gives smooth guide-tone lines.
voicing_rootless_a_about: Third, fifth, seventh and a tension, leaving the root to the bass: Bill Evans’ A voicing.
voicing_rootless_b_about: The same notes starting from the seventh. Alternating A and B keeps the hand in one place through a II–V–I.
voicing_type_a_about: The two-hand voicing from the exercises: root and seventh in the left hand, third, fifth and a tension in the right.
voicing_type_b_about: Root, third and seventh in the left hand, a tension and the fifth in the right.

progress_ungraded: These two modules aren’t graded yet: reading at tempo and keeping a pulse need a fairer measure than a right-or-wrong answer. Their levels stay yours to pick.

settings_reset_confirm: Erase every level, XP and achievement?

achievement_run_25_detail: Twenty-five right answers in a row.
achievement_days_3_detail: Practise three days in a row.
achievement_days_7_detail: Practise seven days in a row.
achievement_days_30_detail: Practise thirty days in a row.
achievement_all_ears_detail: Answer in all five ear-training sub-modules.
achievement_theory_and_ear_detail: Practise both music theory and ear training.
tour_welcome_text: A minute’s tour of where things are. You can skip it now and take it later from Settings.
tour_modules_text: Sight reading, inner rhythm, music theory and ear training. Each card shows your level and how close you are to the next one. Open a module and it explains how it works the first time.
tour_levels_text: In music theory and ear training, levels open one at a time as your answers improve. Progress shows every ladder, your XP and your achievements.
tour_settings_text: Settings holds the language, C D E or Do Ré Mi, chord symbol style, the evening theme, and whether levels open as you progress or all at once.
tour_input_text: Connect a MIDI keyboard on any exercise page to play your answers and have sight reading scored. Without one, the on-screen piano works for every theory and ear question.
tour_start_text: New to jazz harmony? Start with Music theory and its first lesson, then hear the same chords in Ear training. Here for reading? Open Sight reading.
intro_reopen: Show the introduction to this module
intro_place_label: Already know this well? Start at
intro_place_hint: The levels below it count as passed. You can still go back to them.
intro_ungraded_next: This module isn’t graded yet, so every level is yours to choose. Move up when a level feels comfortable at tempo; the results offer a Level up button.
intro_graded_next: Get {required} of your last {window} answers right at a level and the next one opens. Your ladder is on the Progress page.
intro_ear_next: Each sub-module has its own ladder: get {required} of your last {window} answers right at a level and the next one opens.
intro_sight_reading_welcome: Every exercise here is new, so you are always reading and never remembering. Start a level or two below what you play comfortably: fluency at tempo matters more than difficulty.
intro_sight_reading_step_1: Choose your clef or instrument and a level. The exam equivalents under the level help you place yourself.
intro_sight_reading_step_2: Try Practice mode first: the score stays still and nothing is timed.
intro_sight_reading_step_3: Then switch to Performance: a short preview, a count-in, and the music runs at tempo without stopping, as in an exam.
intro_sight_reading_step_4: Connect a MIDI keyboard to have each note checked for pitch and timing.
intro_sight_reading_first: Levels 1 to 3 and the Dandelot guide below: reading from a few landmark notes is the foundation of everything else.
intro_sight_reading_related: Random mute on the metronome trains the same inner pulse as the rhythm module.
intro_rhythm_welcome: This module trains the pulse you carry inside. Nothing is recorded: the app shows the rhythm and keeps time, and you clap, tap or speak it.
intro_rhythm_step_1: Choose Rhythm reading or Polyrhythm, then a level.
intro_rhythm_step_2: Keep the syllables on at first and say them aloud.
intro_rhythm_step_3: Start with the count-in and perform the whole line without stopping.
intro_rhythm_step_4: Lost? Press Listen to hear the rhythm with the chosen feel, then try again.
intro_rhythm_first: Rhythm reading in a straight feel with syllables on; bring in swing once the off-beats sit easily.
intro_rhythm_related: The same pulse carries you through a sight-reading run at tempo.
intro_theory_welcome: This module teaches jazz harmony at the keyboard: three parent scales, their twenty-one modes, the chord on each degree, and how to voice and connect those chords. Every answer is checked as soon as you give it.
intro_theory_step_1: Read the first lesson, on the major scale: seven modes and seven chords.
intro_theory_step_2: Pick an exercise. Name the mode and Name the chord are the gentlest start.
intro_theory_step_3: Answer by choosing, naming, or playing on the on-screen piano or a MIDI keyboard.
intro_theory_step_4: Read the feedback, and hear your answer next to the right one.
intro_theory_first: The lessons in order: the major scale, then melodic minor and harmonic minor, then voicings.
intro_theory_related: Ear training plays the same chords and modes, so you can hear what you learn here.
intro_ear_welcome: Ear training lets you hear what music theory teaches. Every question starts with a reference, a root, a drone or the tonic chord, then plays the question; replay it as often as you like.
intro_ear_step_1: Pick a sub-module: intervals warm the ear up; chords, voicings, modes and progressions are the core.
intro_ear_step_2: Press Start and listen to the reference, then the question.
intro_ear_step_3: Replay freely, and arpeggiate a chord to hear its notes one by one.
intro_ear_step_4: After checking, hear your answer next to the right one.
intro_ear_first: Intervals and chords at Level 1, then modes. The lessons linked above each sub-module explain what you are hearing.
intro_ear_related: Every chord and mode here is taught, with its voicings, in the music theory lessons.

stage_unlock_needs: To open it, reach {percent}% on these exercises of Level {level}: {exercises}

answer_voice: Your voice: say the note names
voice_intro: Read the notes aloud, one name per note, on the beat. Only the name and its timing are graded, not how high or low you say it. Headphones keep the metronome out of the microphone.
voice_setup_needed: Set up the microphone once on this device before your first spoken reading. It takes about 40 seconds.
voice_setup_instructions: Say each name when it lights up, on the click. The seven names come round three times, then seven made-up syllables, so the app learns what isn’t a name.
voice_setup_sequence: You will say the seven names, three times round: {names}. Then seven made-up syllables, once each: {decoys}.
voice_setup_missing: These names were not heard: {names}. Speak a little louder or closer to the microphone, and try again.
voice_mic_denied: The microphone is blocked. Allow it in your browser's site settings, then try again.
voice_mic_unavailable: No microphone was found on this device.
voice_single_staff: Spoken reading uses one staff: the grand staff is read as treble.
voice_slowed: Tempo lowered from {from} to {tempo} so every name can be said clearly (at most 5 names a second).
collect_on: Collection mode is on: every microphone set-up and spoken reading is saved to this computer’s downloads, so recognition can be tuned on real voices. Nothing is sent anywhere.
label_intro: Each note starts as written. Change the ones where you said another name, nothing, or something else, then save the labels next to the recording.
